goldens.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

This is a real source/binary compatibility break for any external implementer of this interface, but the diff does not demonstrate a runtime correctness defect—it's an API change/compatibility concern rather than a bug.

The diff does not include the body of the `if (name == null) { ... }` block, so we cannot verify what exception type/message it previously threw for unknown resource types (it could have been a different exception, or an IllegalStateException with different semantics). adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/RealmAdminPermissionsConfig.java:1416 — myadmin is granted the QUERY_GROUPS admin role unconditionally in the shared realm config, so GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest never exercises the canList()/requireList() forbidden path for a user with zero group-related permissions

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows RealmAdminPermissionsConfig now grants `myadmin` the `AdminRoles.QUERY_GROUPS` role (added alongside `QUERY_USERS`). In `GroupPermissions.canList()`, `canList` returns `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.QUERY_GROUPS) || canView()`, so `myadmin` will always pass `requireList()` even without any group-scoped permissions. The new `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest` uses `myadmin` and asserts empty group results, but that emptiness can come from `.filter(groupsEvaluator::canView)` in `GroupsResource.getGroups()` rather than exercising the forbidden path when `canList()` is false. This is a concrete test-coverage issue created by the role addition, not a functional defect.
